name: @bytescope/mcp

tools.name: detect_file_type
tools.description: Identify a file's real type from its leading bytes (magic numbers), with a confidence level, MIME type and usual extensions. Pass the first few KB of the file; pass the whole file if the format is recognised by its trailer (ZIP, tar). Optionally checks a file name's extension against the detected type.

data.description: The first bytes of the file (4096 is plenty) or the whole file, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

fileName.description: Optional original file name, to check its extension against the content.

fileSize.description: Optional real size of the whole file in bytes, when `data` is only a prefix. Defaults to the length of `data`.

tools.name: hash_bytes
tools.description: Hash bytes with MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512 and/or CRC-32 (the zip/PNG/Ethernet CRC-32/ISO-HDLC). Returns lowercase hex digests.

data.description: The bytes to hash, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

algorithms.description: Which digests to compute. Default: all five.

tools.name: crc_calculate
tools.description: Compute a CRC over bytes, either with a named model from the reveng catalogue (113 models, e.g. "CRC-32/ISO-HDLC", "CRC-16/MODBUS", "CRC-8/SMBUS"; aliases such as "CRC-32" or "MODBUS" work) or with custom Rocksoft parameters.

data.description: The message bytes, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

model.description: Catalogue model name or alias. Default "CRC-32/ISO-HDLC". Mutually exclusive with `params`.

params.description: Custom model. poly/init/xorout as hex strings (normal, MSB-first form) or integers.

tools.name: crc_reverse
tools.description: Recover the CRC model from known message/checksum pairs: first tries every model in the reveng catalogue, then brute-forces 8- and 16-bit polynomials within a time budget. Give at least two samples to avoid coincidental matches.

data.description: The message bytes, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

crc.description: The observed checksum, as hex ("0xCBF43926") or an integer.

tools.name: decode_certificate
tools.description: Decode X.509 certificates and CSRs: subject, issuer, SANs, validity window and status, signature algorithm, public key, key usage, fingerprints. Accepts PEM text (one or many blocks, chains welcome) via `pem`, or DER bytes via `data`. Private keys in the input are classified but never echoed back.

pem.description: PEM text (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE----- …), or a bare base64 DER blob.

data.description: DER-encoded certificate or CSR bytes (instead of `pem`), encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

at.description: Evaluate validity at this ISO 8601 instant instead of now.

tools.name: subnet_calc
tools.description: IPv4/IPv6 subnet calculator: CIDR → network, broadcast (IPv4 only), usable host range, netmask, wildcard, address count and address class/special-range classification. Optionally split the block into equal smaller subnets.

splitPrefix.description: Optional: split into subnets of this prefix length (must be ≥ the block's prefix).

limit.description: Maximum number of split subnets to list.

offset.description: Skip this many split subnets first (decimal string; can exceed 2^53 for IPv6).

tools.name: parse_pcap
tools.description: Parse a pcap or pcapng capture: file summary (format, link types, packet count, time span), a Wireshark-style packet list (protocol, source, destination, info), TCP/UDP stream summaries and protocol hierarchy / conversation statistics. Supports a Wireshark-style display filter such as `tcp.port == 443 && http`.

data.description: The .pcap / .pcapng file bytes, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

offset.description: Skip this many matching packets first.

tools.name: inspect_elf
tools.description: Inspect an ELF binary (executable, shared object, object file, core): header (class, endianness, machine, type, entry point), program headers, section headers, symbol tables, dynamic section (NEEDED libraries, SONAME), notes (build id) and parse warnings.

data.description: The ELF file bytes, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

maxSymbols.description: Maximum symbols listed per symbol table (counts are always exact).

tools.name: parse_intel_hex
tools.description: Map a firmware image: Intel HEX, Motorola S-record or UF2 → contiguous address segments, gaps, start address, record errors (bad checksums, overlaps) and, for UF2, the family ids. Give HEX/S-record as `text`, or any of the three as bytes via `data`.

data.description: Firmware file bytes (required for UF2), encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

tools.name: decode_hid_descriptor
tools.description: Decode a USB HID report descriptor: annotated item listing (like the HID Descriptor Tool), collections, and every input/output/feature report with bit offsets, sizes, usages and logical ranges. Accepts hex such as `05 01 09 06 A1 01 …` or a C array `0x05, 0x01, …` via `descriptor`, or bytes via `data`.

descriptor.description: Descriptor as hex text: "05 01 09 02", "0x05, 0x01," and newlines are all accepted.

data.description: Raw descriptor bytes (instead of `descriptor`), encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

tools.name: parse_exif
tools.description: Read image metadata from a JPEG, PNG or raw TIFF/EXIF block: camera make/model, lens, exposure, ISO, focal length, orientation, capture time, ICC profile presence, plus the list of metadata carriers (EXIF, XMP, ICC, comments, text chunks, trailers) with byte offsets. GPS location is MASKED by default; set includeGps: true to return it.

data.description: The image file bytes, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

includeGps.description: Return GPS coordinates and GPS tags. Off by default: location is personal data.

tools.name: sqlite_schema
tools.description: Read a SQLite database file's structure: every table with its CREATE statement, columns (declared type, primary-key position, NOT NULL, default, foreign-key target) and row count, plus indexes (unique, origin, columns), views, triggers, page size, page count, text encoding, user_version, journal mode and the SQLite version that last wrote the file. Runs no caller SQL and never modifies the file; the engine is SQLite itself (sql.js WebAssembly). Pass the whole file.

data.description: The whole SQLite database file, encoded as base64 (default) or hex. File paths are not accepted.

encoding.description: How `data` is encoded: "base64" (default, standard or URL-safe) or "hex".

tools.name: convert_subtitle
tools.description: Convert subtitles between SRT, WebVTT and ASS/SSA. Detects the source format when `from` is omitted, and reports what the target format cannot carry (styles, positioning, override tags).

tools.name: generate_fixture
tools.description: Generate a real, standards-conformant test file for unit tests instead of hand-assembling bytes: images, archives (including encrypted, split or deliberately corrupted ZIPs), packet captures, self-signed certificates (valid, expiring in N days, expired or not yet valid), audio/video, SQLite, firmware images and PDFs. Every generator is verified by reading its output back with an independent parser. Returns each file as base64 with its name, MIME type and byte length. `options` depends on `kind`: its schema for each kind is the `anyOf` entry whose title is that kind; every option has a default, so {} is valid. Kinds: png (Solid-color PNG (RGB, or RGBA for a translucent color), optional eXIf chunk); jpeg (Solid-color baseline JPEG (YCbCr 4:4:4, standard Huffman tables), optional Exif APP1); gif (Solid-color GIF89a; with frames > 1 an infinitely looping animation cycling colors); bmp (Solid-color 24-bit uncompressed BMP (BITMAPINFOHEADER, bottom-up)); webp (Solid-color lossless WebP (VP8L); VP8X + EXIF chunk when EXIF is requested); zip (ZIP archive: stored or deflated entries, optional ZipCrypto encryption, split segments, or one deliberately corrupted field); pcap (Classic pcap (Ethernet, µs) with a TCP handshake, DNS A query/response or HTTP GET exchange); pcapng (pcapng (SHB + IDB + EPBs, Ethernet, µs) with the same protocol exchanges as pcap); x509 (Self-signed X.509 v3 certificate (ECDSA or RSA) with CN/SAN and a valid, expiring, expired or not-yet-valid window, plus its private key); mp4 (Single-track MP4: H.264 colour bars (I_PCM keyframes + skip frames) or 16-bit PCM sine, moov at the front or the end.); wav (RIFF/WAVE integer PCM with a sine tone or silence, 1-8 channels, 8/16/24/32-bit.); mp3 (Constant-bitrate MPEG-1 Layer III frames that decode to silence, with an optional ID3v2.3 title.); sqlite (SQLite 3 database with the requested tables, columns and row counts; values are a function of the rowid.); elf (Minimal static ELF executable (x86-64, ARM, AArch64 or RISC-V) whose functions call exit(0), with a symbol table.); intel-hex (Intel HEX image with data records, optional extended linear address and start address records.); uf2 (UF2 firmware image in 512-byte blocks with a family id and target address.); pdf (PDF with N labelled pages, exact xref offsets, optional embedded file and optional RC4-40 / RC4-128 / AES-128 encryption.).

kind.description: Which kind of file to generate.

options.description: Options for the chosen kind (see the anyOf entry titled with the kind). Omit for defaults.

anyOf.title: png
anyOf.description: Solid-color PNG (RGB, or RGBA for a translucent color), optional eXIf chunk

exifGpsLatitude.description: GPS latitude in decimal degrees; null writes no GPS IFD

exifGpsLongitude.description: GPS longitude in decimal degrees; null writes no GPS IFD

anyOf.title: jpeg
anyOf.description: Solid-color baseline JPEG (YCbCr 4:4:4, standard Huffman tables), optional Exif APP1

exifGpsLatitude.description: GPS latitude in decimal degrees; null writes no GPS IFD

exifGpsLongitude.description: GPS longitude in decimal degrees; null writes no GPS IFD

anyOf.title: gif
anyOf.description: Solid-color GIF89a; with frames > 1 an infinitely looping animation cycling colors

anyOf.title: webp
anyOf.description: Solid-color lossless WebP (VP8L); VP8X + EXIF chunk when EXIF is requested

exifGpsLatitude.description: GPS latitude in decimal degrees; null writes no GPS IFD

exifGpsLongitude.description: GPS longitude in decimal degrees; null writes no GPS IFD

anyOf.title: zip
anyOf.description: ZIP archive: stored or deflated entries, optional ZipCrypto encryption, split segments, or one deliberately corrupted field

names.description: Entry names; missing ones become file<N>.txt

contents.description: Entry contents (UTF-8); missing ones are generated

fileSize.description: Bytes of generated pseudo-random text per entry; 0 = one short line

volumeSize.description: Split into .z01/.z02/…/.zip segments of at most this many bytes (>= 65536); 0 = no split

corrupt.description: Invert every bit of exactly this field of the first entry / the EOCD

anyOf.title: pcap
anyOf.description: Classic pcap (Ethernet, µs) with a TCP handshake, DNS A query/response or HTTP GET exchange

startTime.description: Timestamp of frame 1 (ISO-8601 or epoch ms); frames are 1 ms apart

anyOf.title: pcapng
anyOf.description: pcapng (SHB + IDB + EPBs, Ethernet, µs) with the same protocol exchanges as pcap

startTime.description: Timestamp of frame 1 (ISO-8601 or epoch ms); frames are 1 ms apart

anyOf.title: x509
anyOf.description: Self-signed X.509 v3 certificate (ECDSA or RSA) with CN/SAN and a valid, expiring, expired or not-yet-valid window, plus its private key

subjectAltNames.description: DNS names, IPv4/IPv6 literals, e-mail addresses or URIs

days.description: expires-soon: expires in N days; expired: expired N days ago; not-yet-valid: starts in N days

now.description: Reference instant (ISO-8601 or epoch ms) for the relative validity modes. Defaults to the server's current time; pass a fixed value for a reproducible certificate.

serial.description: Hex; empty = derived from the key

anyOf.title: mp4
anyOf.description: Single-track MP4: H.264 colour bars (I_PCM keyframes + skip frames) or 16-bit PCM sine, moov at the front or the end.

codec.description: h264 = Constrained Baseline video (plays in browsers); pcm = ipcm 16-bit audio (ISO/IEC 23003-5, demuxers only).

moov.description: front = faststart (moov before mdat); end = moov after mdat.

anyOf.title: wav
anyOf.description: RIFF/WAVE integer PCM with a sine tone or silence, 1-8 channels, 8/16/24/32-bit.

frequency.description: Tone frequency in Hz; must be below sampleRate / 2.

anyOf.title: mp3
anyOf.description: Constant-bitrate MPEG-1 Layer III frames that decode to silence, with an optional ID3v2.3 title.

anyOf.title: sqlite
anyOf.description: SQLite 3 database with the requested tables, columns and row counts; values are a function of the rowid.

tables.description: Row values: INTEGER = rowid, TEXT = '<column>-<rowid>', REAL = rowid + 0.5, BLOB = rowid as 4 big-endian bytes.

anyOf.title: elf
anyOf.description: Minimal static ELF executable (x86-64, ARM, AArch64 or RISC-V) whose functions call exit(0), with a symbol table.

class.description: null = the machine's natural width. arm is 32-only; x86-64 and aarch64 are 64-only.

functions.description: Function symbols; the first one is the entry point.

anyOf.title: intel-hex
anyOf.description: Intel HEX image with data records, optional extended linear address and start address records.

startAddress.description: Entry point as a type-05 record; null for none.

anyOf.title: uf2
anyOf.description: UF2 firmware image in 512-byte blocks with a family id and target address.

anyOf.title: pdf
anyOf.description: PDF with N labelled pages, exact xref offsets, optional embedded file and optional RC4-40 / RC4-128 / AES-128 encryption.

userPassword.description: Printable ASCII. Empty = opens without a prompt but is still encrypted.

ownerPassword.description: Printable ASCII. Empty = same as userPassword.

tools.name: lookup_usb_vendor
tools.description: Look up a USB vendor id (VID) in the linux-usb.org usb.ids database — the same data lsusb uses. Returns the vendor name and its known products, or found: false when the database has no entry.

tools.name: lookup_usb_product
tools.description: Look up a USB product by vendor id and product id (VID:PID) in the linux-usb.org usb.ids database. Returns vendor and product names, or found: false when usb.ids has no such product.

tools.name: lookup_ble_uuid
tools.description: Look up a Bluetooth LE GATT UUID in the Bluetooth SIG assigned-numbers tables (services, characteristics, descriptors) and a list of well-known vendor UUIDs. Accepts 16-bit ("180F", "0x180F"), 32-bit or full 128-bit UUIDs. Returns found: false when no table has it.

tools.name: lookup_hid_usage
tools.description: Look up a USB HID usage in the HID Usage Tables: usage page + usage id → names. Strings are read as hex ("0x0C", "e9"); integers as numbers. Returns found: false when the tables do not name that usage (e.g. vendor-defined pages).

id.description: Usage id within the page: "0xE9", "30" (hex) or 233.

tools.name: lookup_midi_cc
tools.description: Look up a MIDI 1.0 Control Change number (0-127) in the MMA controller assignment table, e.g. 7 → Channel Volume, 64 → Damper Pedal. Returns found: false for numbers the MMA leaves undefined.

tools.name: lookup_midi_manufacturer
tools.description: Look up a MIDI System Exclusive manufacturer id (the byte(s) after F0): one byte 01-7F (e.g. 41 → Roland, 43 → Yamaha) or an extended three-byte id 00 xx xx (e.g. 00 20 29 → Focusrite/Novation). Returns found: false when the MMA table has no such id.

tools.name: lookup_port
tools.description: Look up a TCP/UDP port number in ByteScope's port reference (the well-known service ports developers actually hit: 22, 443, 3306, 5432, 6379, 27017 …): service, transport, whether IANA assigned it, what it is for and its security exposure. Returns found: false for ports the reference does not cover — it is not a full IANA registry.

tools.name: lookup_http_status
tools.description: Look up an HTTP status code in ByteScope's status reference: name, class, defining standard, what it means and how it is confused with its neighbours. Returns found: false for codes the reference does not cover.

tools.name: lookup_file_signature
tools.description: Look up which file formats' magic-number signatures match the given leading bytes, using ByteScope's format catalogue. Every listed segment must be fully covered by the prefix (PNG needs its full 8-byte magic). Returns found: false when no catalogued signature matches. For a verdict with confidence on a real file, use detect_file_type.

instructions: ByteScope: offline file analysis and reference lookups. Binary arguments are base64 (default) or hex strings in `data` with `encoding`; file paths are never accepted. lookup_* tools answer only from their tables and return found: false instead of guessing.
